summary: Bole Alashankou Airport (BPL/ZWBL) serves the city of Bole in the Bortala Mongol Autonomous Prefecture of Xinjiang, China. Situated in a strategic location near the Alashankou border crossing—one of the busiest land ports between China and Kazakhstan—the airport supports both regional connectivity and cross-border commerce. As a medium-sized facility, it primarily handles domestic flights connecting the region to other parts of China.
faqs:
Q: What is the nearest major border crossing to Bole Alashankou Airport?
A: The Alashankou Port, a major rail and road border crossing between China and Kazakhstan, is located near Bole and is one of the most important land crossings in Central Asia.

Q: Does Bole Alashankou Airport handle international flights?
A: The airport primarily operates domestic flights, but its proximity to the Kazakhstan border makes the region strategically important for international trade and travel.

Q: How far is the airport from Bole city center?
A: The airport is located on the outskirts of Bole city, with a relatively short transfer time of approximately 15–20 minutes by road depending on traffic conditions.

Q: What is the best time to visit the Bole area?
A: The most pleasant seasons are late spring through early autumn (May to October), when temperatures are mild and the surrounding landscapes are most accessible.
transport_tips: Taxis and private car hires are the most common ways to reach the airport from Bole city center, as public transit options to the terminal are limited. Travelers heading to or from the Alashankou border crossing should allow extra time, as the border area can experience congestion from freight and passenger traffic. Renting a car with a local driver familiar with the region is recommended for those planning to explore the broader Bortala area.
local_tip: If you're connecting to or from Kazakhstan via the Alashankou border, check the seasonal operating hours of the crossing in advance—winter weather can occasionally cause delays or temporary closures, and having buffer time in your schedule is wise.
